newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-AUSTRALIAN COACH HITS BACK AT CRITICS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-AUSTRALIAN COACH HITS BACK AT CRITICS.

text.p: Australia coach Greg Smith hit back at his media critics and unnamed officials on Friday after saying his job could be on the line in Saturday's Tri-Nations match against South Africa.
Reeling from successive defeats by competition leaders New Zealand, Smith said a defeat in Brisbane could end his chances of coaching the Wallabies next year.
In a hand-written statement delivered to reporters, Smith said the local media and unnamed officials had unfairly treated both himself and his players this season.

"We are being spoken about as though we are some sort of a group of people who really don't know what they are doing and that the person coaching the team doesn't know what he's been doing either," Smith said.
"I think it's very tough on our team," said Smith, who suffered a blow on Friday when lock Garrick Morgan was ruled out with a shoulder injury and replaced by Owen Finegan.

Earlier, writing in a Sydney newspaper column, Smith said: "(Saturday's) test against the South Africans at Suncorp Stadium could well be a determining factor in whether I'm still Australian coach next year.
"I'm under a lot of pressure. Sometimes I wake up in the night and it's on my mind and I have trouble getting back to sleep."

Smith, whose second one-year contract expires at the end of 1997, defended his record this season in tests not involving the All Blacks, who lead the Tri-Nations competition after beating South Africa and Australia away.
In three earlier tests at home this season, Australia twice defeated Five Nations champions France and Triple Crown winners England once to compensate for those losses to New Zealand.

"If we beat the Springboks, we get to a 4-2 situation, with wins over three of the four teams who were rated above us after the 1995 World Cup," wrote Smith, referring to his win-loss record this season.

"I don't think there is anything wrong with that record in international rugby but maybe I'm having myself on," wrote Smith, who took over from Bob Dwyer after Australia's surprise quarter-final World Cup exit two years ago.

Former Wallaby flanker Simon Poidevin this week criticised Smith's tactics as outdated and confused, saying Australia played like a club side in their 33-18 defeat by New Zealand in Melbourne on Saturday.
Other commentators have lamented the constant team changes as Smith has searched for effective scrum and back line combinations.
Of the forwards, only captain and lock John Eales have been constant fixtures this season.

Australia again overhauled their back row when they recalled flankers David Wilson and Matt Cockbain and switched breakaway Daniel Manu to number eight. Morgan's late withdrawal added to the upheavals.
Veteran flyhalf David Knox also came into the side to replace Tim Horan, who has joined fullback Matt Burke and centre Pat Howard on the injury list.
The Springboks, in contrast, made only one change to the side that lost 35-32 to the All Blacks in the series opener on July 19, naming prop Dawie Theron to replace Marius Hurter.
Teams:

Australia - 15-Stephen Larkham; 14-Ben Tune, 13-Jason Little, 12-James Holbeck, 11-Joe Roff; 10-David Knox, 9-George Gregan; 8-Daniel Manu, 7-David Wilson, 6-Matt Cockbain, 5-John Eales (captain), 4-Owen Finegan, 3-Andrew Heath, 2-Michael Foley, 1-Richard Harry.

South Africa - 15-Russell Bennett; 14-Andre Snyman, 13-Percy Montgomery, 12-Danie van Schalkwyk, 11-Pieter Rossouw; 10-Jannie de Beer, 9-Joost van der Westhuizen; 8-Gary Teichmann (captain), 7-Andre Venter, 6-Ruben Kruger, 5-Mark Andrews, 4-Krynauw Otto, 3-Dawie Theron, 2-Naka Drotske, 1-Os du Randt.
